five_day_thesis: The five-day story is a failed breakdown that is now repairing: spot fell to $4,007.8 on 10-26, held the $4,000 put wall, and has added +$66.7 (+1.66%) across three sessions to close the window just -$75.4 (-1.8%) below the 10-22 print of $4,149.9. The regime signal confirms it — window net GEX went +162.99 → -36.17 → -129.17 → -65.70 → +27.03, so dealers spent three sessions amplifying the selloff and have now rotated back to dampening, with the ±$200 pocket improving every day since its -312.95 trough on 10-26. Volatility is deflating alongside it: ATM IV is +0.81pp over the window (19.31% → 20.12%) but -1.24pp off its 21.36% peak on 10-26, so the selloff's premium bid is draining. Positioning tells the same story from both sides — put OI built almost entirely below spot ($3,700 +1,430, $3,950 +1,340, $3,900 +1,213, $3,800 +846) while call OI built just above it ($4,400 +1,282, $4,225 +1,126, $4,300 +987), bracketing price into a tightening $3,950–$4,400 pinch. Both outer walls never moved in five sessions ($3,500 puts, $5,500 calls) and max pain drifted only -$100 (5,500 → 5,400), while total volume halved on both legs (calls 12,955 → 6,625, puts 4,882 → 2,507) — this was hedging, not conviction.
